task.description: TEST-DESIGNER pass (WF-02 Step 3) on REQ-171. ELIXIR-DEV already wrote a substantial test suite (test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs, 38 tests, all passing per SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER's independent reruns). Your job is a MUTATION-DRIVEN review and strengthening pass: read the shipped host_api.ex and capability_gate.ex extension in full, then find and fill real coverage gaps by actually mutating the implementation locally and confirming the existing suite fails to catch each mutation before adding a test that does. Use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching mix commands. Revert every mutation before finishing. Given this is the FIRST requirement with real guest-reachable host functions, mutation coverage on the security-relevant boundaries (memory access, identity attribution, capability gating) matters more than usual here.
acceptance_criteria: Mutate do_read_variable/6 to read from a hardcoded/wrong variables source (or ignore the guest-supplied name and always return a fixed variable) and confirm an existing test catches this.

Mutate do_log/8 to attribute identity fields (script_identity/instance_id/trace_id) from guest-supplied bytes instead of the closure-captured execution_context, and confirm an existing test catches a guest being able to forge its own identity in a log entry -- this is the single most security-relevant mutation in this pass, per SECURITY-REVIEWER's own Step 2c finding.

Mutate write_buffer_result/4 (or wherever the buffer-return protocol writes to guest memory) to skip the MemoryGuard.write/4 bounds check and write directly via a raw call, and confirm an existing test catches a guest-supplied out-of-bounds out_ptr/out_cap no longer being rejected.

Mutate the :none sentinel handling in capability_gate.ex's build_import_table/2 to require an actual capability grant for now/uuid (removing the unconditional-install behavior) and confirm an existing test catches now/uuid becoming ungated-by-default no longer holding under an empty manifest.

Mutate do_now/3 to use a different time source than Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform.now/0 (e.g. DateTime.utc_now/0 directly) and confirm an existing test catches the Lua/WASM parity guarantee breaking (this is the core parity claim AC1/AC4 depend on).

Mutate LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1's call site in host_api.ex to skip the conversion (pass the raw value through some other path) and confirm an existing test catches a subtype-preservation violation -- if this mutation is a no-op given to_lua/1 is currently identity, note that explicitly rather than reporting a false gap.
Do not modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex, capability_gate.ex, or any other implementation file -- test/fixture files only.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.status: COMPLETED -- mutation-driven strengthening pass done. Read host_api.ex/capability_gate.ex in full, then locally mutated the implementation six times per the handoff's acceptance criteria (never committed, always reverted -- diff-confirmed byte-identical to the pre-pass copies after every revert), running the suite against each mutation before deciding whether a new test was needed.

mutations.target: do_read_variable/6 reads a hardcoded name instead of the guest-supplied one

do_log/8 sources script_identity/instance_id/trace_id from guest-decoded context JSON instead of the closure-captured execution_context (fallback to real context only when guest payload omits the key)
mutations.outcome: REAL_GAP_FOUND -- all 19 pre-existing tests kept passing; no test ever sent a context payload shaped like {"script_identity": ...}. This is the SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c finding.
mutations.test: test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs -- "identity fields are never sourced from guest-supplied context bytes -- a guest cannot forge script_identity/instance_id/trace_id" (describe "AC3")

mutations.target: write_buffer_result/4 skips MemoryGuard.write/4, calls Wasmex.Memory.write_binary/4 directly
mutations.outcome: PARTIAL_GAP_FOUND -- moderately-out-of-bounds positive out_ptr (memory_size+100) still returns -2 under the mutation because wasmex's own internal bounds check also rejects it, so existing tests couldn't distinguish MemoryGuard running from wasmex's own check catching it. A negative i32 out_ptr (attacker-chosen large-unsigned address) diverges: real code returns clean {:ok,[-2]}, mutant traps and returns {:error, "...wasm backtrace..."}.
mutations.test: test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs -- "now: a negative (attacker-chosen large-unsigned) out_ptr is still rejected as -2, not a raw wasmex trap"

mutations.target: capability_gate.ex build_import_table/2 :none sentinel -- filter clause removed so :none rows require an actual capability grant
mutations.outcome: ALREADY_CAUGHT -- 16/38 tests failed including capability_gate_test.exs's existing "REQ-171: :none-gated rows (now/uuid) are present even with an empty manifest" and "an empty capability list produces exactly the :none-gated rows, nothing else"

mutations.target: do_now/3 calls DateTime.utc_now/0 directly instead of Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform.now/0
mutations.outcome: ALREADY_CAUGHT -- AC4 parity test failed immediately (mutant ignores the injected FixedTimeSource double)

mutations.target: LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 call site skips the conversion
mutations.outcome: NO_OP_CONFIRMED, NOT_A_GAP -- to_lua/1 is `def to_lua(value), do: value`, a bare identity function; no call site mutation can change observable behavior. Reported explicitly per the handoff's own instruction rather than manufacturing a false gap.
